Uncle Nearest is a premium American whiskey brand, best known for Uncle Nearest 1856 Premium Whiskey and 1884 Small Batch Whiskey, named after Nearest Green, the formerly enslaved distiller who taught Jack Daniel. It sells bottled Tennessee whiskey to consumers through liquor stores, bars, restaurants and online, and owns the Nearest Green Distillery in Shelbyville, Tennessee. Founded in 2017 by Fawn Weaver, it is Black-founded and has raised substantial private funding, including a 2024 round near $225 million. It is a fast-growing consumer spirits brand with strong awareness among US whiskey drinkers.

Verifone is one of the world's largest makers of point-of-sale payment terminals, offering card readers, countertop and mobile terminals, the Carbon smart-POS line, and payment software, gateway and processing services for merchants. Customers are retailers, restaurants, banks, acquirers and fuel and transport operators in over 150 countries, paid through hardware sales and recurring software and services fees. Founded in 1981, it is privately held after the 2018 take-private by Francisco Partners and was later restructured, with Griffin Investment Partners among later owners. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness beyond seeing its terminals at checkouts.

7AI is a Boston-based cybersecurity startup that sells an AI-driven security operations platform using autonomous AI agents to triage and investigate alerts for security teams. Customers are enterprises and security operations centres that want to automate analyst work, paid through software subscriptions. The company emerged from stealth in 2025 with a large seed round and then a Series A, bringing total funding to roughly $200 million. It is an early-stage B2B software company with little public brand awareness. Limited details are confirmed beyond its AI-agent security positioning.

Aetion is a New York-based health-data software company that provides real-world evidence analytics, letting pharmaceutical firms, regulators and payers analyse healthcare claims and electronic records to measure how treatments perform outside clinical trials. Its Aetion Evidence Platform is sold by subscription and services to life-sciences companies and public health bodies. Founded in 2013, it raised over $200 million in venture funding and was acquired by Datavant in 2025. B2B healthcare data business with low public brand awareness.

Amplience is a London-based software company offering a composable content management and digital experience platform for retailers and brands, including its dynamic content and media delivery tools, now with generative AI features. Customers are mid-size and large e-commerce and fashion brands who use it to produce and deliver product content across websites and apps; revenue comes from SaaS subscriptions. Founded in 2008 in the UK with offices in the US, it has raised over $200 million, largely from growth investors. B2B technology with little consumer awareness.

Arrived Homes is a Seattle-based real estate investing platform that lets everyday investors buy fractional shares in single-family rental homes and vacation rentals from as little as $100, with the company handling property management and distributing rental income. Backed by Jeff Bezos's investment arm Bezos Expeditions, it was founded in 2019 and has raised about $200 million in funding. Revenue comes from fees on the properties it sells shares in. A consumer fintech and proptech app with moderate awareness among US retail investors.

Blacklane is a Berlin-based chauffeur service offering pre-booked, fixed-price rides in premium vehicles through its app and website, mainly for airport transfers, business travel and hourly hire, in around 50 countries and about 300 cities. Customers are business travellers, corporate accounts, hotels and airlines, with revenue earned as a commission or margin on rides delivered by a network of professional drivers. Founded in 2011, it has raised about $200 million from investors including Daimler. A premium B2C and B2B travel brand with good awareness among frequent business travellers.

Chrono24 is the world's largest online marketplace for luxury watches, connecting private sellers and professional dealers with buyers in more than 100 countries, with several hundred thousand listings including Rolex, Patek Philippe and Audemars Piguet. It earns commissions and listing fees, and offers an escrow-style payment service. Founded in 2003 and headquartered in Karlsruhe, Germany, it employs around 700 people and took a major investment from General Atlantic in 2021. Well-known consumer brand among watch enthusiasts and an obvious fit with premium luxury sponsorship.

DeFi Technologies is a Toronto-based financial technology company that bridges traditional finance and decentralised finance, with an asset management arm (Valour, issuing crypto exchange-traded products listed in Europe), plus digital asset trading and venture investments. Customers are retail and institutional investors seeking crypto exposure, and revenue comes from management fees and trading and staking income. It is publicly listed on Nasdaq and the Cboe Canada exchange under the ticker DEFI. Niche investor-facing brand with limited mainstream consumer awareness. Funding shown reflects equity raises.

Directed Capital is a St. Petersburg, Florida financial services firm that Crunchbase describes as a national commercial asset workout and special situations lender and investor. It works with distressed or complex commercial assets and borrowers, and raised debt and equity funding of about $215 million. It is a niche B2B finance business, with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Distyl AI is a San Francisco-based enterprise AI company that builds and deploys custom generative AI systems and agent workflows for large corporations, working alongside client teams to embed AI in core operations. Customers are Fortune 500-scale firms in sectors such as telecoms, healthcare and financial services, paid through software and implementation engagements. Founded in 2022 by former Palantir staff, it raised about $175 million in 2025 and roughly $200 million in total. B2B with little public brand awareness.

Empower Semiconductor is a Milpitas, California chip company developing integrated voltage regulators and power-management chips, notably its Crescendo product that shrinks and speeds up power delivery for AI accelerators, data centres and high-performance computing. Customers are chip designers and server and AI-hardware makers, with revenue from semiconductor sales. Founded in 2017, it raised about $140 million in 2025 and over $200 million in total. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Exodigo is an Israeli-founded, Palo Alto-based technology company that uses non-intrusive sensors and AI to produce 3D images of what lies underground, mapping utilities, pipes and cables before construction or excavation. Customers are utilities, civil engineering and construction firms, transport agencies and developers, paid for per-project subsurface mapping services. Founded in 2019, it has raised roughly $212 million, including a large 2025 round. B2B deep-tech with little consumer brand awareness.

Fairplay is a Mexico City fintech offering performance-based financing to e-commerce and digital businesses, lending against sales and marketing performance so sellers can fund inventory and advertising. Customers are online merchants and consumer brands in Latin America, and revenue comes from fees and interest. It has raised around $200 million in a combination of equity and debt funding. B2B finance with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Fundamental Global is a Florida holding company, formed by the 2024 merger of FG Financial Group and FG Group Holdings, that Crunchbase describes as a reinsurance and investment business. It combines reinsurance, merchant banking, asset management and other holdings, and is listed on Nasdaq under FGF. Led by Kyle Cerminara, with funding shown of about $213 million. It is a B2B financial holding company with little consumer brand awareness.

GlobalWafers is a Taiwan-listed maker of silicon wafers, the base material for semiconductors, supplying chipmakers worldwide with polished, epitaxial and SOI wafers plus silicon carbide wafers. It acquired the US wafer maker MEMC (formerly SunEdison Semiconductor), whose operations are in Saint Peters, Missouri, shown as the location here, and has expanded in Texas with US CHIPS Act support. One of the top four wafer suppliers globally. B2B materials supplier with little public brand awareness.

Guzman Energy is a Denver-based wholesale power provider and energy developer in the western US, selling electricity to rural electric cooperatives and municipal utilities and developing solar, wind and storage projects, including a deal to acquire coal-plant assets and transition them to renewables. Founded in 2016 by Rob Guzman, it has raised around $210 million in financing. Revenue comes from wholesale power sales. B2B utility business with limited public brand awareness. Funding shown is mainly project and growth capital.

K-Way is an Italian outerwear brand famous for its packable, waterproof jackets, originally created in Turin in 1965. It sells through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale across Europe, Asia and the US, aimed at casual and urban consumers, and has been part of the Italian group BasicNet (which also owns Kappa and Superga) since 2004. Crunchbase lists a London address and funding of about $202 million. Strong consumer brand awareness in Italy and Europe.

LegalOn Technologies is a legal technology company offering AI-powered contract review and drafting software that flags risks, suggests edits and tracks deals, used by in-house legal teams and law firms. Founded in Tokyo in 2017 as LegalForce, it has a large user base in Japan and expanded to the US from its San Francisco office. Revenue is from SaaS subscriptions, and it has raised about $200 million in funding including a 2023 round of $50 million. B2B software with limited public brand awareness.

LootMogul is a Delaware-registered technology company describing itself as a vertical AI voice and agent platform. Previously known for a sports and celebrity gamified fan-engagement app, it pivoted toward conversational AI agents and has raised roughly $208 million according to Crunchbase, a figure to verify. Customers are enterprises needing voice agents, with revenue from software. Limited consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Lyte Fiber is a Houston-based fibre-to-the-home internet provider, building gigabit and multi-gigabit broadband networks in Texas and neighbouring states for residential and business customers, and selling subscriptions for high-speed internet. Founded in 2020 as a startup within the Lyte group, it has raised nearly $200 million in equity and debt to fund its fibre rollout. Regional consumer telecom brand with limited awareness beyond its footprint.

MMP Capital is a Farmingdale, New York financial services firm that, per Crunchbase, offers financial solutions to employees, likely including payroll-linked services, and has raised about $212 million. Beyond that the company is not clearly known. It appears to be a niche B2B or B2B2C finance business with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Moneyfarm is a digital wealth manager that offers investment portfolios and pension products to retail savers in the UK, Italy and Germany, built around goals-based advice, ETFs and human advisers, with over 100,000 clients and more than 5 billion euros in assets under management. Founded in Italy in 2011 and headquartered in London, it is majority-owned by Poste Italiane following a 2024 deal, having also been backed by Allianz and United Ventures. Revenue is from management fees. Moderate consumer brand awareness in its markets.

Moneyview is an Indian digital lender and personal finance app, headquartered in Bengaluru, that offers personal loans, credit-line products and money-management tools to salaried and self-employed borrowers, with millions of downloads. Revenue is from interest and fees. Founded in 2014 as Whizdm, it has raised about $200 million from investors including Apis Partners and Peak XV, and holds an NBFC licence after acquiring a lending licence. Consumer-facing fintech with moderate brand awareness in India.

Morse Micro is an Australian semiconductor company based in Sydney that designs Wi-Fi HaLow (802.11ah) chips, giving Wi-Fi long range and very low power for IoT devices such as cameras, sensors, smart-home and industrial equipment. Customers are device makers and module vendors, with revenue from chip sales. Founded in 2016 as a spin-out from the University of Sydney and UNSW, it has raised about $205 million in venture funding, including a 2025 round. B2B with little consumer awareness.

Nana is a Saudi quick-commerce and grocery delivery platform from Riyadh, offering app-based delivery of groceries and household items from partner stores and dark stores to consumers in Saudi Arabia, plus the pharmacy and health items. Founded in 2016, it is one of the leading grocery apps in the kingdom and has raised over $200 million, including Series C money from investors such as Tiger Global. Revenue is from order margins and delivery fees. Well-known regional consumer brand.

Neiman Marcus Group is the US luxury department store operator, running Neiman Marcus, Bergdorf Goodman and Last Call stores and online, selling designer apparel, accessories, beauty and home goods to affluent shoppers. Founded in 1907 in Dallas, it has around 36 full-line stores and a big e-commerce business, and was acquired by Saks Global (the combination of Hudson's Bay's Saks with Neiman Marcus) in 2024. Previously owned by Ares and CPPIB after a 2013 buyout. Strong luxury consumer brand awareness in the US.

Orchid Island Capital is a Florida-based mortgage real estate investment trust (REIT) that invests in agency residential mortgage-backed securities guaranteed by Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae, financed with repo borrowing and earning net interest spread. It is externally managed by Bimini Advisors, listed on the NYSE as ORC, and pays monthly dividends to investors. Founded in 2010. A financial investment vehicle sold to investors and with no consumer brand awareness.

PolyAI is a conversational AI company, founded in Cambridge/London in 2017, that builds voice assistants handling customer service calls for enterprises such as hotels, restaurants, banks and utilities, automating bookings and enquiries in many languages. Revenue comes from platform subscriptions and usage. It raised a $86 million Series D in 2025, bringing total funding to over $200 million, with investors including Georgian and NVentures. B2B software with limited consumer awareness; HQ listed as San Francisco in the input.

Qventus is a Mountain View company providing AI-driven automation software for hospitals and health systems, helping them optimise surgery scheduling, patient flow, discharge planning and capacity so that staff spend less time on administrative tasks. Customers are US hospitals and health networks, paid via subscription. Founded in 2012, it has raised about $200 million in venture funding, including a 2025 round of $105 million. B2B healthcare software with little consumer awareness.

Remixpoint is a Japanese company, listed in Tokyo (ticker 3825), that describes itself as an electric services firm. Its business centres on retail electricity supply, power trading and energy services, with additional recent activity in cryptocurrency holdings and used-car/e-commerce ventures. It has issued capital shown here as 31.5 billion yen in funding. Moderate profile in Japan's small-cap market, with little consumer brand awareness internationally. Details beyond the electricity business are not confirmed.

Rimag is a Chinese medical imaging services company, described in the input as Shenzhen-based though the listed headquarters is Beijing. It offers cloud-based medical imaging services and data services, and Crunchbase lists funding of about $200 million. Its customers are likely hospitals and imaging centres. Little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Rural Development Partners is an Iowa-based finance company, based in Clear Lake, which Crunchbase says is eligible to apply for annual tax-credit allocations, suggesting it is a community development entity channelling investment into rural projects. It has raised about $205 million. It appears to be a niche B2B community finance business, with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

RWB is the merged business of Wildberries and Russ, the operator of Russia's largest e-commerce marketplace, Wildberries, which sells fashion, electronics, home goods and more online through a vast network of pickup points and warehouses, also covering logistics and payments. The merger was announced in 2024 and closed in 2025, combining Wildberries with Russ (which runs businesses including the Russ Outdoor advertising firm). Founded by Tatyana Bakalchuk and based in Moscow, serving tens of millions of customers in Russia and neighbouring markets. Very high consumer visibility in Russia and CIS. Sanctions and Russian-market considerations apply for sponsorship.

TELUS Health is the health technology division of Canadian telecom group TELUS, offering electronic medical records, pharmacy and claims-management software, virtual care, and employee wellbeing and assistance services (including the former LifeWorks business) to employers, insurers, clinics and governments. It serves hundreds of millions of people worldwide and is based in Vancouver. TELUS itself is listed on the TSX and NYSE as T and TU. B2B and B2B2C healthcare brand; moderate recognition in Canada.

Tendo is a Philadelphia-based healthcare software company building a platform that connects patients, providers and health systems, with digital front-door tools for scheduling, communication and payments on top of electronic records. Its aim is a trusted connection between patients and the healthcare organisations that serve them. The company has raised about $207 million in funding. B2B healthcare software with little public brand awareness; further details were not confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

The Good Glamm Group is an Indian digital-first beauty and personal-care company that built a portfolio through acquisitions, including MyGlamm, POPxo, ScoopWhoop, Sirona, Organic Harvest, St Botanica and BabyChakra, mixing content, community and D2C products. Founded in 2021 by Darpan Sanghvi, it became a unicorn in 2022 after raising about $214 million overall from investors such as Warburg Pincus and Bessemer. It suffered a severe liquidity crisis, layoffs and brand sell-offs from 2024. Well-known beauty brands among younger Indian consumers.

Verint Systems is a customer experience automation software company based in Melville, New York, selling AI-powered contact-centre, workforce engagement, speech analytics and bot tools to large enterprises and governments worldwide. Listed on Nasdaq as VRNT, it generates about $900 million in annual revenue and employs around 3,500 staff. Thoma Bravo agreed to take it private in 2025 in a deal worth about $2 billion. B2B software with little consumer brand awareness.

Westgate Resorts is the Orlando-based timeshare and vacation ownership company founded by David Siegel, operating resorts in Florida (Orlando, Gatlinburg area), Las Vegas, Branson, Park City, Williamsburg and elsewhere, and selling points-based timeshare interests plus hotel stays. It is privately owned and operates dozens of resorts with thousands of units. The Crunchbase entry lists funding of about $206 million. Strong brand presence in US leisure markets, with travel and destination appeal for sponsors.

Actelis Networks is a Sunnyvale-based telecom equipment maker selling hybrid fibre-copper networking gear that delivers fast broadband over existing copper wire and fibre, targeting smart cities, transport, military and utilities. Customers are network operators, governments and defence bodies, paid through hardware and software sales. It is listed on Nasdaq under ASNS since 2022 and operates its main engineering in Israel. B2B with no consumer awareness.

Antithesis is a Vienna, Virginia-based software testing startup that uses a deterministic simulation approach to find bugs in distributed systems and AI-written code, letting engineering teams replay and reproduce failures. Founded by former FoundationDB engineers, it raised a $105 million Series A in 2025, bringing funding to about $182 million. Customers are software engineering organisations, paid by subscription. B2B developer tool with little public brand awareness.

Auterion is an open-source drone software company, with US headquarters in Arlington, Virginia and Swiss origins, whose operating system (AuterionOS) and Skynode hardware run fleets of military and commercial drones. Customers include the US Department of Defense, NATO allies and Ukraine-related programmes, and it has raised about $181 million, including a 2025 round. Revenue is from software and hardware. B2B defence technology with limited consumer awareness.

Beekeeper is a Zurich-based digital workplace and employee communication app built for frontline workers in industries such as hospitality, retail, manufacturing and logistics, bringing messaging, task management, shift scheduling and training to staff without desks. Sold by subscription to enterprises, it was founded in 2012 and has raised about $180 million. It merged with Staffbase in 2025 (announced) to create a larger employee app player. B2B software with low consumer brand awareness.

Blackline Safety is a Calgary company making connected gas detectors and wearable devices (G7 and G6 monitors) that alert safety teams to gas exposure, falls and emergencies, plus cloud software for tracking workers. Customers are oil and gas, utilities, chemicals, mining and construction firms, paid through hardware and subscriptions. Listed on the Toronto exchange as BLN, it was founded in 2004 and operates in about 100 countries. B2B industrial safety brand with limited consumer awareness.

CallMiner is a Waltham, Massachusetts software company that sells conversation intelligence, analysing recorded calls, chats and emails with AI to help contact centres improve service, compliance and sales (its Eureka platform). Customers are large enterprises such as banks, insurers and retailers, paid by subscription. Founded in 2002, it has raised about $197 million, including a growth equity investment from Sound Ventures, Insight Partners and others. B2B tech with little consumer awareness.

Cameo is a Chicago-based marketplace where fans pay celebrities, athletes and creators for personalised video messages, and for business shout-outs and fan interactions. Founded in 2016, it takes a commission on each booking, with thousands of talent on the platform, and has raised about $190 million, including backing from Kleiner Perkins and Lightspeed. It went through layoffs and cost cuts in 2023. Strong consumer brand awareness in the US and high relevance to sports and entertainment talent.

Crisp is a retail data platform based in Bentonville, Arkansas, close to Walmart's headquarters, that ingests and standardises daily sales, inventory and supply chain data from retailers so that consumer packaged goods brands can see what is selling and where. Customers are food, beverage and CPG brands and distributors, paid by subscription. Founded in 2017, it has raised about $187 million. B2B software with little consumer awareness.

Endor Labs is a Palo Alto application security company that helps software teams detect and fix risks in open-source dependencies, code and AI-generated code, with tools including reachability analysis to cut false alerts. Customers are engineering and security teams at tech and financial enterprises, paid by subscription. Founded in 2021, it raised a $93 million Series B in 2025, taking total funding to roughly $188 million. B2B cybersecurity with limited public brand awareness.

Farcaster is a decentralised social network protocol and app ecosystem, with the main client Warpcast, that lets users own their identities and posts via Ethereum, popular with crypto developers and creators. Its parent company, Merkle Manufactory (San Francisco/Los Angeles), raised $150 million in a 2024 round led by Paradigm, taking total funding to about $180 million. Revenue is limited, from storage rent and token-related products. In 2025 the Farcaster team was acquired by Neynar. Niche consumer crypto brand.

Federato is a San Francisco insurtech selling an AI-powered underwriting platform, RiskOps, that helps commercial and specialty insurers prioritise risks, select the best accounts and price them quickly. Customers are carriers and managing general agents, paid by software subscription. Founded in 2020, it raised $100 million in a 2025 Series D, bringing funding to about $180 million. B2B software with no consumer awareness.

Foodics is a Riyadh-based restaurant management software company whose cloud point-of-sale, inventory, reporting and payments tools run thousands of restaurants, cafes and retailers across Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt and other Middle East markets. Customers are food-service operators, paid by subscription and payments fees. Founded in 2014, it has raised about $198 million, including a 2022 Series C led by Sanabil and STV. B2B software, well known among regional restaurateurs but with little consumer awareness.

Guzman y Gomez is an Australian quick-service Mexican restaurant chain, serving burritos, tacos and nachos from over 200 restaurants, mainly in Australia, with a few in Singapore, Japan and the US. Founded in 2006 in Sydney by Steven Marks and Robert Hazan, it is a consumer food brand with drive-thrus and high brand awareness in Australia. It listed on the ASX as GYG in June 2024. Revenue is from company-owned and franchised restaurants. Attractive consumer brand for sponsors in Australia.

Hawk (Hawk AI) is a Munich-based software company selling AI-based anti-money-laundering, fraud and transaction-monitoring systems to banks, payment firms and financial institutions, available as cloud software. Founded in 2018, it raised a $56 million Series C in 2025, bringing funding to about $190 million. Customers are mid-size and large financial institutions in Europe, North America and Asia. B2B compliance technology with little consumer awareness.

HIR Casa is a Mexican real estate financing company, based in Mexico City, offering home and development financing, including loans for residential property builders and mortgage products, funded partly by investors and debt. Funding is shown as 3.675 billion pesos. It is a niche finance business and a known name mainly within Mexico's housing sector, with little consumer brand awareness. Details of scale were not confirmed.

Honasa Consumer is the Indian beauty and personal-care company behind Mamaearth, The Derma Co, Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, Ayuga and BBlunt, selling mostly through online, marketplace and modern retail channels. It is based in Gurugram and was founded in 2016 by Varun and Ghazal Alagh. It listed on the NSE and BSE in November 2023 (ticker HONASA) and has annual revenue of roughly 2,000 crore rupees. Strong consumer brand awareness among young Indian shoppers.

Kiwi is a New York fintech that provides tools to establish and build credit; the Crunchbase line is short, and the company is not clearly known. It has raised about $191 million. It appears to be a consumer-oriented credit-building product, though the details and customers were not confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Legacy Group Capital is a Bellevue, Washington private lender, described by Crunchbase as providing loans and capital to businesses and real estate borrowers. It has raised about $180 million to fund lending. Little more is known about its products, customers or scale. It is a niche B2B finance firm with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Lumafield is a San Francisco hardware and software company that makes Neptune, an affordable industrial CT scanner, plus Voyager analysis software, letting engineers look inside parts and products to inspect quality and find defects. Customers include manufacturers in aerospace, automotive, medical devices and consumer goods. Founded in 2019 by veterans of Mars and other firms, it raised about $67 million in 2025, bringing funding to roughly $190 million. B2B industrial technology with little consumer awareness.

Luminary Cloud is a San Mateo, California physics AI company offering a cloud platform that speeds up engineering simulation for design in aerospace, automotive and manufacturing, using GPUs and machine learning to replace slow traditional computational fluid dynamics. Founded in 2021 by former Google and Nvidia staff, it has raised about $187 million, including a $72 million Series B in 2025. Customers are engineering teams. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Marvel Fusion is a Munich-based developer of laser-driven fusion energy technology, using nanostructured targets and ultra-short, high-power lasers to aim for commercial fusion power. Founded in 2019, it has raised a Series B of about 113 million euros in 2025 and is building laser facilities with Colorado State University in the US. Funding shown is around 165 million. Revenue is minimal, since it is pre-commercial research-stage. Deep-tech energy company with little consumer brand awareness.

MatchMove Pay is a Singapore fintech that provides embedded finance and wallet services, including prepaid cards, digital wallets and banking-as-a-service, to businesses and consumers in Southeast Asia and India. Customers are corporates and platforms building payment programmes, with revenue from fees. Founded in 2009, it has raised roughly $183 million. B2B fintech brand with modest recognition in its markets and little mainstream consumer awareness.

Nan Fung Group is a Hong Kong family-owned conglomerate founded in 1954 by the Chen family, focused on property development and investment across Hong Kong, mainland China and overseas (including London and Singapore), plus investment arms in technology and finance. It owns commercial buildings such as Nan Fung Place and sponsors the Nan Fung Life Sciences fund. Funding shown is 1.5 billion Hong Kong dollars. Well known in Hong Kong business circles, with limited consumer brand awareness.

PostHog is a San Francisco-based open-source product analytics platform that gives engineers one toolset for analytics, session replay, feature flags, A/B testing, surveys and data warehousing. Customers are over 100,000 software teams and startups, charged on usage. Founded in 2020 through Y Combinator by James Hawkins and Tim Glaser, it is known for its radical transparency and humorous branding, and has raised about $182 million. B2B developer brand with strong recognition among tech workers.

Pryon is a Raleigh, North Carolina company that sells enterprise knowledge management and AI search software, letting organisations in defence, healthcare, manufacturing and finance ask questions of their documents and receive sourced answers. Founded in 2017 by Igor Jablokov, formerly of Pittsburgh Pattern Recognition, it has raised about $180 million. Revenue is from enterprise licences. B2B software with little consumer brand awareness.

R2 is a Mexico City embedded lending platform that offers capital and credit tools to businesses through partner platforms, plus corporate lending. It has raised about $180 million in a mix of equity and debt. Customers are merchants and fintech platforms in Latin America. B2B finance with low public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Revolution Race is a Swedish performance outdoor and cycling apparel brand from Borås, known for multi-functional garments, mainly for mountain biking, trail running and skiing, sold direct-to-consumer online in Europe and elsewhere, with a stylish technical design. Funding is shown as around 1.8 billion Swedish kronor. Founded in 2011, it is an e-commerce focused brand with a loyal following among outdoor sports enthusiasts and some visibility in sports communities.

Rhode Island Infrastructure Bank is a quasi-public state financing agency, based in Providence, that provides low-interest loans and financing to support clean water, drinking water, energy efficiency, roads and bridges, and other infrastructure projects for municipalities in Rhode Island. It is a government-related entity and has raised about $177 million in funds, including state-backed bond financing. B2B and public sector with no consumer brand awareness.

SBFC Finance is a Mumbai-based non-banking finance company that offers secured small-business loans, loans against property and gold loans to small enterprises and self-employed borrowers in India's smaller cities, through a branch network in many states. It listed on the NSE and BSE in August 2023 under the ticker SBFC, following investment by Bain Capital and others. Revenue is from interest income. Regional financial brand with modest visibility.

Semgrep is a San Francisco application security company whose platform scans source code, dependencies and secrets to find vulnerabilities, built on an open-source static analysis engine popular with developers. Customers are software and security teams at technology and financial firms, paid by subscription. Founded in 2017 as r2c, it has raised about $193 million, including a 2025 Series D. B2B developer security brand known among engineers but with little consumer awareness.

SEON is a Hungarian-founded fraud-prevention company, now listed with an Austin, Texas headquarters, whose platform assesses digital footprints to detect fraud, scams and money laundering for online businesses. Customers include fintechs, payment firms, iGaming operators and e-commerce companies, paid by subscription. Founded in 2017, it raised a $80 million Series C in 2025, bringing funding to about $188 million. B2B software, with some brand profile in iGaming and fintech.

Swimlane is a Denver security automation company that sells a low-code platform for security orchestration, automation and response, which helps security teams respond to alerts faster using AI. Customers are large enterprises and government agencies, paid by software subscriptions. Founded in 2014, it raised a $45 million round in 2025, bringing funding to about $182 million. B2B cybersecurity with little consumer awareness.

UltraGreen.ai is a Singapore-based company that Crunchbase describes as a pioneer in healthcare intelligence, applying artificial intelligence to the healthcare sector. It has raised about $188 million in funding. Few other details of its products, customers or scale are available from the input. B2B healthcare technology with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Virgin Hotels Las Vegas is a lifestyle resort hotel and casino just off the Strip, opened in 2021 in the former Hard Rock Hotel building and part of Richard Branson's Virgin Hotels brand. It has around 1,500 rooms, restaurants, a pool, a casino and a live-music venue, The Theater. Revenue comes from rooms, gaming, and food and beverage. Crunchbase shows funding of about $190 million. Strong consumer awareness through the Virgin name.

Virtru is a Washington, D.C. data protection company providing email and file encryption and data-centric security software, including a Data Security Platform based on the Trusted Data Format, which lets organisations control access to shared data. Customers are government agencies, defence contractors, healthcare and finance firms, paid by subscription. Founded in 2012 by Will Ackerly and John Ackerly, it has raised about $190 million. B2B security brand with little consumer awareness.

VitalHub is a Toronto-listed healthcare software company (TSX: VHI) providing electronic patient records, case management, patient flow and mobile tools to health systems and mental health providers, chiefly in the UK (NHS) and Canada. Revenue is from software licences and subscriptions, and it grows through acquisitions. Funding is shown as around 270 million Canadian dollars. B2B healthcare IT with little consumer brand awareness.

You.com is a San Francisco AI search company founded in 2020 by Richard Socher and Bryan McCann, offering an AI assistant, search engine and APIs for enterprises and developers, with research and agent tools. It raised $100 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in 2025 and about $195 million in total. Revenue is from subscriptions and enterprise API sales. A tech brand with some consumer awareness though far behind the major search engines.

Parker is a New York fintech offering corporate credit cards and spend management designed for e-commerce brands, with credit limits based on revenue and cash flow instead of personal guarantees. Founded in 2020 by Yaniv Mehr, it raised around $177 million in funding including debt facilities, but it shut down its operations in 2024-25 following a financial collapse. The row came from a search of listed companies and shows funding of about $116 million. The input does not provide products, customers or scale, so specifics were not confirmed. Likely a B2B ingredients supplier with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Calavo Growers is a Santa Paula, California company that sources, packs and distributes fresh avocados and other produce, and produces guacamole and prepared foods through its Fresh and Renaissance Food Group segments. It sells to retailers, food-service operators and processors in the US and abroad, and is listed on Nasdaq under CVGW. Founded in 1924 as a growers' cooperative. Known in produce aisles for its avocado and Fresh-Cut brands, with moderate consumer awareness.

CIMG is a Nasdaq-listed company, formerly NuZee, known for single-serve pour-over coffee and private-label coffee manufacturing, with a Tuen Mun, Hong Kong address in this record. Customers are retailers and consumers buying coffee and related goods. Crunchbase lists funding of about $73 million. It is a small company with limited consumer brand awareness. Its current product mix after the rename was not confirmed.

Digital Brands Group is an Austin, Texas fashion company that owns direct-to-consumer apparel brands including Bailey 44, DSTLD, Harper & Jones and Stateside, selling online and through wholesale and a few stores. Listed on Nasdaq under DBGI, it has built its portfolio through acquisitions, with revenue around $15 million and heavy losses. Customers are fashion consumers in the US. Small niche brands with limited awareness.

El Pollo Loco is a fast-casual restaurant chain, headquartered in Costa Mesa, California, known for fire-grilled citrus-marinated chicken, with over 490 restaurants, mostly in California and the Southwest, about a third franchised. Listed on Nasdaq under LOCO, it has annual revenues around $470 million. Customers are quick-service diners. Strong regional consumer brand in the western US with limited national awareness.

Flow Alkaline Spring Water, from Flow Beverage Corp, is an Ontario-based company selling naturally alkaline spring water in recyclable cartons and bottles, plus flavoured and functional waters, through grocery and retail chains in Canada and the US. Based in Aurora, Ontario, it was listed on the TSX Venture exchange. Revenue is from beverage sales to consumers. Funding of about $63 million is shown. Growing premium water brand, with moderate awareness in Canada.

Jahez International Company is a Saudi online food-delivery and quick-commerce app, based in Riyadh, connecting consumers with restaurants and other merchants through its own driver network, and expanding into other Middle East markets. It listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) in 2023. Revenue comes from commissions and delivery fees. Crunchbase shows funding of about $76 million. Well-known consumer brand in Saudi Arabia, with strong sponsorship potential in the region.

Liuliumei is a Chinese snack-food brand based in Wuhu, Anhui, known for plum-based snacks sold through retail and online channels across China. The record came from a search for listed companies and shows funding of about 504 million yuan. Customers are consumers buying packaged snacks. Details of scale and listing are not confirmed. Recognisable snack brand in China with limited international awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Maison Solutions is a Monterey Park, California grocery operator that runs Asian-American and Hispanic supermarkets in Southern California, including Good Fortune Supermarket and Greenland Market, and offers delivery. It was listed on Nasdaq under MSS in 2023, and generates revenue of about $200 million from store sales. Customers are local community shoppers. Regional retail business with limited awareness beyond Southern California.

Pague Menos is a Brazilian pharmacy and drugstore retail chain based in Fortaleza, Ceara, selling medicines, health and beauty products, and operating more than 1,500 stores in all Brazilian states, including the Extrafarma brand following a 2014 acquisition. Listed on B3 under PGMN3. Customers are Brazilian consumers, with revenue mainly from store sales. Strong regional consumer brand in Brazil, especially the north and north-east.

Sotherly Hotels is a Williamsburg, Virginia hotel real estate investment trust that owns upscale and full-service hotels, mainly in the US South and Mid-Atlantic, operated under brands such as Hilton, Marriott and DoubleTree. Listed on Nasdaq under SOHO. Revenue is from hotel operations. Funding of about $77 million is shown. B2B and investor-facing, with little consumer brand awareness of its own.

Torrid is a City of Industry, California retailer of plus-size women's clothing, lingerie and accessories, selling through about 650 stores in the US, Canada and Puerto Rico and online, in sizes 10 to 30. Founded in 2001 as a Hot Topic concept, it was spun off and listed on the NYSE as CURV in 2021. Revenue is around $1.1 billion. Strong consumer brand in the US plus-size fashion market.

TUI Group is the world's largest leisure travel company, headquartered in Hanover, Germany, combining tour operators (TUI), airlines (TUI fly), hotels and resorts (Riu, TUI Blue, Robinson), cruises (TUI Cruises, Marella Cruises, Hapag-Lloyd Cruises) and the TUI Musement activities platform, selling holidays to tens of millions of customers, mainly in Europe. Revenue is roughly 23 billion euros. Listed in London and Frankfurt. Very strong consumer brand in the UK and Germany.

Galaxy Gaming is a Las Vegas company that creates and licenses proprietary casino table games and side bets, such as Lucky Ladies and Bonus Blackjack-style wagers, along with electronic table-game systems, to casinos worldwide. It is a small listed company, and revenue comes from licence and lease fees paid by casino operators. B2B gaming supplier with little consumer brand awareness. Funding shown is about $47 million. Ownership changes in recent years were not confirmed.

Holaluz is a Barcelona-based Spanish electricity and solar company that sells renewable-sourced power and rooftop solar installation to households and businesses, along with a community-sharing platform for solar surplus, and has a few hundred thousand customers. Founded in 2010, it is listed on BME Growth in Madrid and was an early B Corp. Revenue is from electricity retail and solar. Moderate consumer brand awareness in Spain.

Karat Packaging is a Chino, California maker and distributor of disposable foodservice products including cups, lids, takeout containers, straws and eco-friendly compostable packaging, plus cutlery, gloves and janitorial items, sold to restaurants, cafes and distributors across the US. Listed on Nasdaq under KRT, with annual revenue around $400 million. Founded in 1976. B2B supplier with little consumer awareness.

CubicFarm Systems is a Chilliwack, British Columbia agricultural technology company selling automated indoor vertical growing systems that produce hydroponic livestock fodder and, previously, leafy greens. Customers are farmers and livestock producers, and revenue comes from equipment sales and subscriptions. Listed on the TSX under CUB, with funding of about $36 million shown. Its financial position has been under strain in recent years. B2B agtech with little consumer awareness.

DAVIDsTEA is a Montreal-based specialty tea retailer, selling loose-leaf teas, tea bags, teaware and accessories online and through stores, mainly in Canada. Founded in 2008, it was listed on Nasdaq under DTEA from 2015, and restructured under Canadian creditor protection in 2020 and has since reduced its store count. Customers are consumers, and funding of about C$35 million is shown. Well-known consumer brand in Canada, with a smaller US presence.

Fanhua Inc. is a Guangzhou-based Chinese financial services and insurance intermediary, formerly called CNinsure, distributing life and property insurance products through agents and its digital platforms. It was listed on Nasdaq under FANH. Customers are Chinese individuals and businesses buying insurance, and revenue comes from commissions. Funding of about $32 million is shown. Moderate brand profile in China, with little international consumer awareness.

Giglio Group is a Milan-based fashion and luxury e-commerce services company that runs online stores for brands, also offering logistics and a digital media platform, with some Nasdaq listing history under GIGL alongside its Italian listing. Customers are fashion brands and retail shoppers. Funding of about 24.5 million is shown. Small-scale B2B2C business with limited consumer brand awareness. Current status of the listing was not confirmed.

KITS Eyecare is a Vancouver-based online retailer of contact lenses, eyeglasses, sunglasses and eye care products in Canada, which started as a mail-order contact lens retailer. Listed on the TSX under KITS, it was a small consumer e-commerce company with funding of about $27 million. Customers are consumers buying eyewear online. Moderate consumer awareness in Canada. Further details of ownership and scale were not confirmed.

Mulberry is a British luxury fashion house, founded in 1971 in Somerset, famous for leather handbags such as the Bayswater and Alexa, plus accessories and clothing, made largely at its Somerset factories. It sells through its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale. Listed on London AIM, its main shareholders have been Challice (the Christina Ong family) and Frasers Group. Strong luxury brand in the UK and Asia, with a premium customer base.

Ryde Group is a Singapore carpooling and ride-hailing app operator that connects riders with private-car and taxi drivers, along with a delivery and advertising business. It is listed on the NYSE American under RYDE after a 2023 IPO. Customers are Singapore commuters and corporate clients, and funding of about $32 million is shown. Revenue is from commissions and fees. Consumer app with moderate brand awareness in Singapore.

Caesars Entertainment is the largest casino-entertainment company in the US, operating about 50 resorts under brands such as Caesars Palace, Harrah's, Horseshoe and Eldorado, and the Caesars Sportsbook and online casino business, serving gamblers across the US. It was formed in 2020 when Eldorado Resorts bought Caesars, and is listed on Nasdaq as CZR, with annual revenue near $11 billion. It sponsors major sport properties and has a very strong consumer brand.

JUUL Labs is a San Francisco maker of electronic cigarettes (vapes), known for the compact JUUL device and nicotine pods, which dominated the US e-cigarette market in the late 2010s. It was backed by Altria, which took a 35 percent stake in 2018 for about $12.8 billion, later written down, and was the subject of regulatory action and large settlements over youth vaping. It received FDA marketing authorisation in 2025. Highly recognised consumer brand, though tobacco-related restrictions limit sponsorship.

WeWork is a New York flexible workspace company that rents shared office space, private offices and memberships to freelancers, startups and corporates, with locations in cities around the world. Founded in 2010 by Adam Neumann, it was backed by SoftBank, abandoned its 2019 IPO, listed via SPAC in 2021, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023. It emerged as a private company in 2024. Strong brand awareness among professionals.

BYJU'S is a Bengaluru-based Indian education technology company, founded in 2011 by Byju Raveendran, known for its learning app with video lessons, tutoring and test prep aimed at school students, and for acquiring Aakash, WhiteHat Jr, Great Learning and Epic. It once ranked among India's most valuable startups, sponsored the Indian cricket team and FIFA World Cup, and has since faced insolvency proceedings and unpaid debts. Very high consumer brand awareness in India, though financially distressed.

Cousins Properties is an Atlanta-based real estate investment trust that owns, develops and manages Class A office towers and mixed-use properties in Sun Belt cities including Atlanta, Austin, Charlotte, Phoenix, Tampa and Nashville. Its tenants are corporates, and it is listed on the NYSE under CUZ with a market value of several billion dollars. Founded in 1958. Investor and B2B real estate business with little consumer brand awareness.

Eni Plenitude is the retail energy and renewables arm of Italian energy group Eni, selling electricity, gas, and energy services to millions of customers in Italy, France, Spain and other European markets, with renewable generation capacity and a network of electric-vehicle charging points through Be Charge. Headquartered in San Donato Milanese, near Milan, and partly owned by outside investors including Ares, it plans a public listing. A recognised utility brand in Italy, with consumer-facing visibility.

GEMS Education is a Dubai-founded operator of private K-12 schools, started by the Varkey family, running dozens of schools in the UAE and further afield, with several hundred thousand students and international curricula. Crunchbase gives a London address. Revenue is from tuition fees, and funding of about $3.4 billion is shown, which should be verified. Known mainly in the Gulf and among expatriate parent communities, with moderate consumer awareness.

Rexford Industrial Realty is a Los Angeles real estate investment trust that owns and manages industrial properties, such as warehouses and logistics buildings, in infill Southern California markets. It leases to e-commerce, logistics, manufacturing and entertainment tenants. Listed on the NYSE under REXR, it is one of the largest pure-play industrial REITs in Southern California, with a market value of many billions of dollars. Investor-facing business with little consumer brand awareness.

South Bow is a Calgary-based liquids pipeline company spun out of TC Energy in October 2024, operating the Keystone Pipeline system that carries Canadian crude oil to US Gulf Coast and Midwest refineries, plus the Marketlink and Grand Rapids pipelines. Listed on the TSX and NYSE under SOBO, it earns regulated and contracted transport fees from producers and shippers. B2B energy infrastructure with limited consumer brand awareness.

Stef is a French specialist in temperature-controlled logistics and transport, running refrigerated warehouses and a truck fleet that moves fresh and frozen food for retailers and manufacturers across Europe, with maritime activity under Stef Seafood. Headquartered in Paris, it is listed on Euronext Paris, with about 20,000 employees and revenue of several billion euros. Customers are food companies and supermarkets. B2B with little public brand awareness.

Tenglong Holding Group is a Beijing-based Chinese company that, according to Crunchbase, provides global distributed data centres and data storage services. Funding of about $3.7 billion is shown, which is a large figure and worth verifying. Its customers, scale and ownership are not otherwise detailed in the input. Likely a B2B infrastructure business with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Adevinta was a Norwegian-listed online classifieds group, headquartered in Amsterdam, operating marketplaces such as leboncoin in France, Marktplaats in the Netherlands, mobile.de and Kleinanzeigen in Germany, Milanuncios and InfoJobs in Spain, and Subito in Italy. It was taken private in 2024 by Permira and Blackstone in a deal worth about 14 billion euros. Revenue comes from listings, advertising and subscriptions. Strong consumer brand awareness in its European markets.

American Bath Group is an Irving, Texas manufacturer of bathroom products, including bathtubs, showers and related fixtures under brands such as Aquatic and Lasco Bathware, selling to home improvement chains, builders and distributors in North America. It is privately held, and Crunchbase shows funding of about $2.3 billion. B2B supplier, mostly sold through retail partners, with low consumer brand awareness. Details of ownership were not confirmed.

ASFINAG is the Austrian state-owned company responsible for planning, financing, building, operating and tolling the country's motorway and expressway network of about 2,300 kilometres, including the vignette and truck toll systems. It is wholly owned by the Republic of Austria and based in Vienna. Revenue comes from tolls. Public infrastructure operator, familiar to drivers in Austria though not a consumer product brand.

B.TECH is an Egyptian consumer electronics and household appliance retailer, based in Cairo, selling TVs, phones, laptops, white goods and furniture through a large network of stores and online, with consumer financing. Founded in 2003, it has around 150 stores in Egypt and is expanding into Saudi Arabia, after an IPO on the Egyptian Exchange. Well-known consumer retail brand in Egypt, with funding of about $1.8 billion shown, which should be verified.

BKW is a Bern-based Swiss energy and infrastructure group, one of Switzerland's largest energy companies, that generates and sells electricity, including hydro and nuclear power, and offers engineering, planning and building services plus grid operation for infrastructure, buildings and energy projects. Customers are households, businesses and municipalities, mainly in Switzerland, with international engineering work. Majority owned by the Canton of Bern and listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange. Recognised utility brand in Switzerland, with little consumer-sponsorship profile.

Builders FirstSource is the largest US supplier of building materials, manufactured components and construction services to professional homebuilders, remodelers and contractors, selling lumber, trusses, windows, doors, millwork and installation, from more than 500 locations across the US. Headquartered in Irving, Texas, and listed on the NYSE under BLDR, with annual revenue around $15 billion. Formed from the 2015 merger with ProBuild. B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Gibraltar Industries is a Buffalo, New York manufacturer of building products, including residential mail and storage products, ventilation, renewable energy racking and structures for solar, and agtech greenhouse and infrastructure. Customers are home improvement retailers, builders, utilities and solar developers, and it is listed on Nasdaq under ROCK. Revenue is around $1.1 billion. B2B and retail-channel supplier with modest consumer brand awareness.

HNI Corporation is a Muscatine, Iowa maker of workplace furnishings and residential building products, with brands including HON, Allsteel, Kimball International and Gunlocke in office furniture, and Hearth & Home brands such as Heatilator, Heat & Glo and Quadra-Fire fireplaces. It sells through dealers, retailers and builders in North America, and is listed on the NYSE under HNI, with revenue around $2.5 billion. B2B and retail brands with modest consumer awareness.

Hudson Pacific Properties is a Los Angeles real estate investment trust that owns office properties in West Coast cities and film and television studios, including Sunset Studios in Hollywood, Sunset Gower and Sunset Las Palmas, leased to tech companies and entertainment firms. Listed on the NYSE under HPP, it is one of the largest studio landlords in Hollywood. Revenue comes from rent. Investor and B2B real estate business with little consumer brand awareness.

Independence Realty Trust is a Philadelphia-based apartment real estate investment trust that owns and operates multifamily communities, around 30,000 units, in non-gateway US markets such as Atlanta, Dallas and Memphis. Revenue is from rent paid by residents. It is listed on the NYSE under IRT, with funding of about $1.7 billion shown in Crunchbase. Investor-facing real estate business with little consumer brand awareness beyond local apartment communities.

Inspired Education Group is a global premium private schools operator, with more than 100 schools in about 30 countries across Europe, Africa, the Americas, Asia and Australia, serving tens of thousands of students from kindergarten through university. Founded in 2013 by Nadim Nsouli, it is privately owned by Brookfield-related and other investors, and its head office is in London while this record shows Sydney. Revenue is from tuition. Known to affluent parents, with moderate consumer awareness.

Kilroy Realty is a Los Angeles real estate investment trust owning and developing Class A office, life science and mixed-use properties in coastal West Coast markets, including Los Angeles, San Francisco, San Diego, Seattle and Austin. Tenants include technology, media and life science companies. Listed on the NYSE under KRC, it has a market value of several billion dollars. Revenue is from rent. Investor and B2B business with little consumer brand awareness.

LeEco, formerly Letv, is a Beijing-based Chinese internet and consumer electronics conglomerate founded by Jia Yueting, known for streaming video, smart TVs, smartphones and electric vehicles through its LeSEE concept and links to Faraday Future. It expanded to the US and agreed to buy TV maker Vizio in 2016, then collapsed financially in 2017 with huge debts. Its listed arm Leshi Internet was delisted. Once a very high-profile Chinese consumer brand, now largely defunct or restructured.

Stahl-Holding-Saar is a Dillingen, Saarland holding company for the Saarland steel industry, owning the steelmakers Dillinger (heavy plate) and Saarstahl (wire rod and bar steel), and related engineering and services businesses. It is owned largely by Saarland foundation and shareholder structures, and has several thousand employees. Customers are industrial buyers in energy, construction and automotive. Funding of about 1.7 billion is shown. B2B steelmaker with little consumer awareness.

Transgrid is the operator of the high-voltage electricity transmission network in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory, owning and operating about 13,000 kilometres of lines and substations. It is based in Sydney and is privately owned by a consortium of institutional investors. Revenue comes from regulated network charges. It is involved in major energy-transition projects. Infrastructure operator with limited consumer brand awareness.

Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield is a Paris-based developer and operator of flagship shopping destinations, owning malls such as Westfield London, Westfield Stratford City, Westfield Forum des Halles, Westfield Century City, and Westfield Mall of Scandinavia, across Europe and the US, plus offices and convention centres. Revenue is mainly from rents on retailers, with hundreds of millions of annual visitors. Listed on Euronext Paris and Amsterdam under URW. Strong consumer-facing mall brand, with an advertising and sponsorship platform.

Walker & Dunlop is a Bethesda, Maryland commercial real estate finance company that originates and services multifamily and commercial mortgage loans, including Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and HUD products, along with brokerage and investment management. Listed on the NYSE under WD, it is one of the largest multifamily lenders in the US. Customers are property owners and developers. B2B finance with limited consumer brand awareness.

Weyerhaeuser is a Seattle-based timber real estate investment trust and one of the world's largest private owners of timberlands, with over 10 million acres in the US, plus wood products manufacturing producing lumber, oriented strand board and engineered wood. Customers are homebuilders and building-supply dealers. Founded in 1900 and listed on the NYSE under WY. Revenue is around $7 billion. B2B, with little consumer brand awareness beyond its name.

Aspen Insurance Holdings is a Bermuda-based specialty insurance and reinsurance group with operations in Bermuda, London and the US, writing property, casualty, specialty and reinsurance for businesses globally. Listed on the NYSE under AHL, it has long been a Lloyd's market participant and was previously owned by Apollo funds. Japan's Sompo agreed in 2025 to acquire it for about $3.5 billion. B2B insurer with little consumer awareness. Funding shown is about $1.15 billion.

Bulgarian Energy Holding is the state-owned energy holding company of Bulgaria, based in Sofia, grouping power generation including the Kozloduy-linked and coal sectors, the national electricity system operator, the gas company Bulgargaz, Bulgartransgaz gas transmission and the Maritsa East mines. It is owned by the Bulgarian government. Customers are utilities, industry and households. Large national energy group with little consumer sponsorship profile outside Bulgaria.

Elsewedy Electric is an Egyptian industrial group based in New Cairo that makes wires and cables, electrical products, transformers, meters and infrastructure, and runs power-plant and turnkey engineering projects, with operations across the Middle East, Africa and Asia. Founded in 1938 and listed on the Egyptian Exchange, it employs more than 20,000 people. Customers are utilities, contractors and governments. Well-known B2B brand in the region, with limited consumer awareness.

JD Property is the infrastructure asset manager within JD.com's logistics business, based in Beijing, that owns and manages logistics parks and warehouses used by JD Logistics and third parties, and raises funds backed by logistics real estate. Crunchbase shows funding of about $1.5 billion. Customers are e-commerce and supply chain operators. B2B real estate arm of a consumer internet group, with low independent brand awareness.

JX is the Japanese non-ferrous metals business associated with JX Nippon Mining & Metals, now JX Advanced Metals, which mines and smelts copper, and produces electronic materials such as sputtering targets and rolled copper foil for semiconductors and electronics. JX Advanced Metals listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in March 2025. The location here is Bekasi, Indonesia, likely a local operation. B2B materials supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Nice Tuan, also known as Xingsheng Youxuan, is a Chinese community group-buying e-commerce platform that sells fresh produce and groceries at low prices to households, who order via the app and pick up from neighbourhood stores. Based in Beijing, it was valued above $1 billion in the community group-buying boom and later cut operations. Revenue is from product sales. Known to Chinese consumers, with limited visibility abroad.

Reddit is a San Francisco online platform of topic-based communities (subreddits) where users post, comment and vote, with hundreds of millions of monthly visitors. It earns revenue from advertising and from licensing its content for AI training, including deals with Google and OpenAI. Founded in 2005 and listed on the NYSE under RDDT since its March 2024 IPO. Very high consumer brand awareness among young, internet-native audiences, with growing brand marketing.

The Rural Electrification Agency is a Nigerian federal government agency based in Abuja, responsible for expanding electricity access to rural communities, funding mini-grids, solar home systems and energy projects through programmes such as the Nigeria Electrification Project with World Bank support. Funding of about $1.6 billion is shown. Customers are rural households and developers. Public-sector body with no commercial sponsorship profile.

Almosafer is a Saudi online travel agency and part of Seera Group, offering flights, hotels, packages and holiday bookings across the Middle East, along with the Tajawal brand. Based in Riyadh, it serves Gulf travellers and tourists and earns commissions and fees. Seera Group is listed on the Saudi Exchange. One of the best-known travel brands in the region, with strong consumer awareness and sponsorship potential in Saudi Arabia.

Artea Bank, formerly Siauliu Bankas, is a Lithuanian bank headquartered in Vilnius, providing retail and business banking, payments, leasing and financing, mainly in Lithuania. It is listed on the Nasdaq Vilnius exchange and is the country's third largest bank. Customers are consumers and small and medium companies. Regional banking brand with moderate awareness in Lithuania.

Convoy was a Seattle digital freight network that matched truckload shipments with trucking carriers using an app and algorithms, backed by Bezos Expeditions, Jeff Bezos and Marc Benioff, and valued at about $3.8 billion in 2022. It abruptly shut down in October 2023 after running out of cash, and Flexport acquired its technology and customer relationships. Funding raised was about $1.1 billion. B2B logistics technology with limited consumer awareness, now defunct.

Equatorial Energia is a Brazilian electricity company based in Brasilia that distributes power in northern and northeastern states such as Maranhao, Para, Piaui, Alagoas and Amapa, and also has transmission and renewable assets plus the water and sanitation business. It is listed on the B3 under EQTL3 and serves millions of customers. Customers are households and businesses in its concession areas. Utility brand with regional awareness in Brazil.

K Wave Media is a Korean-focused media and entertainment company, with a Grand Cayman registered address, that Crunchbase says develops content and franchises tied to the Korean wave, including music, television and fan experiences. Funding of about $1.0 billion is shown, which should be verified. Specific shows, artists, ownership and scale were not confirmed. Likely entertainment brand with moderate awareness among K-culture fans. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Perch is a Boston-based consumer brands aggregator that acquired and scaled third-party sellers on Amazon, buying direct-to-consumer and Amazon brands in categories such as home, pets and personal care. Founded in 2019, it raised funds in equity and debt of about $909 million, at one point operating dozens of brands. The Amazon aggregator sector contracted sharply after 2022. B2B2C holding business with low consumer awareness of its parent name.

Proterra was a Burlingame, California maker of battery-electric transit buses and battery systems, selling Proterra Catalyst buses to city transit agencies and batteries to commercial vehicle makers. It listed via SPAC in 2021 and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in August 2023, after which the transit business was sold to Phoenix Motor and the battery unit to Volvo. Funding of about $1.1 billion is shown. B2B and public transit, with low consumer awareness; now defunct as an independent firm.

Scopely is a Culver City, California mobile game developer and publisher behind Monopoly Go!, Marvel Strike Force, Star Trek Fleet Command, Stumble Guys and Yahtzee With Buddies, with hundreds of millions of installs. It was acquired in 2023 by Saudi-owned Savvy Games Group for $4.9 billion and bought Niantic's games business in 2025. Revenue is from in-app purchases and advertising. Strong brand among mobile gamers, and a heavy marketer, including sports sponsorships.

Tupperware Brands is the Orlando-based maker of reusable plastic food storage and kitchen products sold mainly by direct selling through independent consultants and parties, in dozens of countries. Founded in 1946 by Earl Tupper, it is listed on the NYSE as TUP. After years of financial difficulty it filed for Chapter 11 in September 2024 and its assets were taken over by lenders. Iconic consumer brand with very high recognition, but now financially fragile.

UnionBank of the Philippines is a major Philippine universal bank based in Pasig City, offering retail, corporate and digital banking, with a strong fintech and digital-first reputation, including its mobile app and payment products. Listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange under UBP, it is part of the Aboitiz Group. Customers are consumers, businesses and government. Well-known domestic bank brand with a sizeable sponsorship presence in the Philippines.

ACM Research is a Fremont, California maker of single-wafer wet cleaning, plating and stress-free polishing equipment used in semiconductor manufacturing, with major operations in Shanghai, and customers among Chinese and global chipmakers. Listed on Nasdaq under ACMR, it earns revenue from equipment sales and services, with annual revenue near $800 million. B2B equipment supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

ALLO Communications is a Nebraska-based fibre broadband, TV and phone provider that builds fibre-to-the-home networks in communities in Nebraska, Colorado, Arizona and Missouri, often in partnership with municipalities. Headquartered in Imperial per Crunchbase, with a large presence in Lincoln, it has raised about $866 million in equity and debt. Customers are households and businesses. Regional consumer telecom brand, well known in the communities it serves.

AM Green Group is an Indian green energy developer based in Hyderabad, building large-scale green hydrogen, ammonia and renewable energy projects, including a major complex at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, for export to Europe and domestic customers. It is associated with the GreenKo group's founders and has raised about $760 million in equity. Revenue is expected from green ammonia and power sales. B2B energy developer with little consumer brand awareness.

Amlak International Finance is a Saudi Arabian finance company based in Riyadh that offers business financing and real estate finance, notably in the property and leasing sectors. It is listed on the Saudi Exchange. Funding of about SAR 2.9 billion is shown. Customers are individuals and companies seeking finance, and revenue comes from financing income. Limited consumer brand awareness outside Saudi Arabia.

Amtrak, the National Railroad Passenger Corporation, is the US government-supported intercity passenger rail operator, running long-distance trains and the Northeast Corridor services including Acela, from its Washington, D.C. headquarters. It carries about 30 million passengers a year across roughly 500 destinations in 46 states and parts of Canada, and receives federal funding. Revenue is from ticket sales and state-supported routes. Strong consumer awareness in the US.

ATI, formerly Allegheny Technologies, is a Dallas-based producer of specialty materials and components, including titanium and nickel alloys, superalloys and forgings for aerospace, defence, energy and medical customers. Listed on the NYSE under ATI, with annual revenue around $4.5 billion. Its largest customers are jet engine and aircraft manufacturers. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand awareness.

Brightline Trains is a Miami-based passenger rail operator running higher-speed intercity trains between Miami, Fort Lauderdale, West Palm Beach and Orlando, with a planned extension to Tampa, plus Brightline West between Las Vegas and Southern California. Owned by Fortress Investment Group's rail business, formerly Florida East Coast Industries. Revenue comes from ticket sales and real estate. Strong consumer brand in Florida, with growing visibility.

CABB is a German-headquartered producer of fine chemicals and agrochemical intermediates, including chloroacetic acid and derivatives, supplying agriculture, pharmaceutical, personal care and industrial customers worldwide from plants in Germany, Switzerland and elsewhere. Crunchbase lists it at Sulzbach, and funding of about 625 million. It is privately owned by an investor group. B2B chemicals supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Cenomi Centers, formerly Arabian Centres Company, is the largest mall owner and operator in Saudi Arabia, running lifestyle shopping malls such as Hayat Mall and Salaam Mall, leasing space to retailers and offering advertising. It is part of the Cenomi group, backed by Fawaz Alhokair family, and listed on the Saudi Exchange. Based in Riyadh. Revenue is from rents. Strong consumer-facing mall brands, with sponsorship and media assets.

Chemtrade Logistics is a Toronto-based supplier of industrial chemicals and services, including sulphuric acid, sodium chlorate, water treatment chemicals and regeneration of spent acid, to customers across pulp and paper, mining, oil refining and water treatment in North America. Listed on the TSX under CHE.UN, with revenue around C$1.6 billion. B2B chemicals business with no consumer brand awareness.

Deezer is a Paris-based music streaming service with a catalogue of more than 120 million tracks, offering free and paid subscriptions, personalised Flow recommendations and podcasts in about 180 countries. Founded in 2007, it listed on Euronext Paris in July 2022 and counts around 9 million subscribers. Revenue is from subscriptions and advertising. Strong brand in France and parts of Europe and Latin America, though smaller than Spotify.
